<!-- This file is generated by tools/Picket.Docs. -->

Picket evaluated Cl100k byte-pair encoding as additional evidence for the
native `p(random)` model. The candidate does not ship because it did not
improve holdout discrimination and materially increased runtime and
distribution costs.

## Candidate

The candidate adds two normalized features to the existing eleven-feature
logistic model:

- token density: Cl100k token count divided by UTF-8 byte count,
- mean token rank: the mean Cl100k token identifier divided by the mergeable
  vocabulary size.

Token density describes segmentation efficiency. Mean token rank is a bounded
proxy for how late the token's byte sequence appears in the merge vocabulary;
it is not a probability or a provider-specific credential signal.

[`scripts/Evaluate-BpeRandomness.cs`](https://github.com/willibrandon/picket/blob/main/scripts/Evaluate-BpeRandomness.cs)
fits the baseline and candidate against the same deterministic corpus used by
`picket-random-v1`. Both use 1,024 training samples per class and an independent
holdout with 256 samples per class. The evaluator pins
`Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers.Data.Cl100kBase` 2.0.0 and keeps it outside every
shipping project.

The quality gate requires at least one percentage point of random or structured
recall lift, with no regression in accuracy, likely-random precision, or either
recall metric. A lower Brier score alone is insufficient because randomness
thresholds use the two recall regions and secret detection must fail toward
retaining findings.

Reproduce the evaluation and verify the reviewed decision with:

```powershell
dotnet run --file ./scripts/Evaluate-BpeRandomness.cs -- --verify
```

## Quality

The deterministic holdout result is:

| Metric | Existing model | BPE candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Accuracy at 0.5 | 0.998047 | 0.998047 |
| Brier score | 0.014483 | 0.014087 |
| Precision at `likely-random` | 1.000000 | 1.000000 |
| Recall at `likely-random` | 0.937500 | 0.937500 |
| Recall at `likely-structured` | 0.906250 | 0.875000 |

The candidate leaves accuracy, likely-random precision, and likely-random
recall unchanged. It moves eight additional structured samples out of the
`likely-structured` region, a 3.125 percentage-point recall regression. The
small Brier-score improvement does not offset that regression.

## Runtime And Distribution

Measurements were taken on Windows 11 build 26200.8875, an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X,
.NET SDK 10.0.301, and .NET runtime 10.0.10. BenchmarkDotNet 0.15.8 measured a
deterministic 48-character alphanumeric value after tokenizer initialization:

| Measurement | Existing model | BPE candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean time per finding | 1.039 us | 2.034 us | 1.96x |
| Managed allocation per finding | 320 B | 1,064 B | 3.33x |

Reproduce the microbenchmark with:

```powershell
dotnet run --file ./scripts/Benchmark-BpeRandomness.cs -- -f "*"
```

Separate minimal `win-x64` Native AOT probes measured initialization and
distribution overhead. Startup is elapsed process-start time through the first
stdout line after five warmups, over 30 samples. Working set is sampled after
that line while the process remains alive:

| Measurement | Baseline probe | BPE probe | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup median | 17.351 ms | 37.550 ms | +20.199 ms |
| Startup p95 | 19.137 ms | 41.492 ms | +22.355 ms |
| Working-set median | 7,749,632 B | 34,119,680 B | +26,370,048 B |
| Working-set p95 | 7,942,144 B | 34,254,848 B | +26,312,704 B |
| Native AOT executable | 933,376 B | 3,325,440 B | +2,392,064 B |

The probe pair differs only by the pinned tokenizer data dependency,
initialization, and evaluation of token count and rank for one value. The
executable-size comparison excludes PDBs and package-cache files.

## Decision

The BPE candidate is rejected. It adds no detection lift on the committed
holdout, weakens structured recall, nearly doubles per-finding time, more than
triples managed allocation, adds about 25 MiB of working set, and adds about
2.28 MiB to the minimal Native AOT executable. Reconsideration requires a new
candidate and corpus evidence that clear the quality gate before distribution
cost is weighed.
